abstract: New distribution records, from which range shifts are inferred, arise only when a species is present, someone is looking, and the observation is written up. Here we build a species × province × year risk set for 1,029 new bird records in China (2002–2024) and model the annual hazard of a first record with a discrete-time proportional-hazards formulation. Dating records to publication rather than discovery biases inference: publication lags discovery by a mean of 2.09 years, re-dating changes the year of 83.1% of events, and cuts the survey-effort coefficient by 37% while leaving accumulated warming unchanged. After correction, accumulated warming relative to a species' historical range (hazard ratio 1.36 per SD, 95% CI 1.22–1.52) and survey effort (1.40, 1.25–1.58) contribute comparably and interact negatively (0.85, 0.76–0.95). Design-preserving permutation nulls place both outside their nulls (P = 0.005), but the warming null is centred on 1.157, not unity, so the increment from species-specific referencing is about 1.18; the effort effect collapses to 0.980 when its temporal alignment with events is broken. A province-by-year random intercept, the largest variance component, raises conditional discrimination from 0.72 to 0.85 and conditional R² from 0.27 to 0.41. The marginal return on effort declines from 2.18 in 2002 to 1.07 in 2024 while the warming effect does not; new records fall disproportionately east (36.9%) and north-east (27.9%) of species' range centroids. Documented range gains reflect climate and observation in roughly equal measure, and the date attached to a record determines which appears to dominate.

budget_check:
GCB hard constraints: main text (Introduction + Materials and Methods + Results + Discussion) ≤ 8,000 words; abstract ≤ 250 words, unstructured single paragraph, no citations; IMRaD with Methods placed after the Introduction.

Source totals: Introduction 672 + Methods 1,437 + Results 6,246 + Discussion 833 = 9,188 words, i.e. 1,188 over the cap — a 12.9% cut, matching the brief's "about 13%".

Target allocation (sum of the target_words column above):
  Introduction                 620   (−52)
  Materials and Methods      1,400   (−37)
  Results (13 subsections)   4,754   (−1,492)
  Discussion                   833   (0)
  ------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                      7,607   (−1,581 from source)

Results arithmetic: 420 + 236 + 680 + 210 + 230 + 300 + 700 + 250 + 128 + 500 + 260 + 300 + 540 = 4,754, just under the 4,800 the brief allows for Results.

Headroom against the cap: 8,000 − 7,607 = 393 words (4.9%). Deliberately retained, for three reasons. (1) Section headings, in-text display-item callouts and the displayed equation are counted by some editorial-office counters and not by others; a 5% buffer removes the risk of an over-length desk return. (2) GCB reviewers routinely ask for one or two added sentences of interpretation, and the Discussion is where they belong — no second round of triage needed. (3) Moving Methods ahead of Results means the Methods must read standalone for someone who has not yet seen the Results, which typically costs 20–40 words of added signposting at typesetting.

Where the 1,492 Results words come from: Results 7 (−420), Results 10 (−262), Results 13 (−235), Results 6 (−155), Results 11 (−117), Results 5 (−89), Results 12 (−46), Results 1 (−37), Results 8 (−17), Results 4 (−14), Results 3 (−8). Results 2 and Results 9 are untouched at 236 and 128 words. The four protected conclusions live in Results 2 and 3 (i), Results 4 and 5 (ii), Results 9 plus the province-level passage of Results 7 (iii), and Results 8 (iv); the three heaviest cuts all fall outside those passages except Results 7, whose province-level diminishing-returns paragraph is explicitly preserved word for word.

Display items: 27 enumerated in the source (9 tables + 18 figures) plus 5 further items cited in the text (Extended Data Tables 1–2, Figs P1–P3) = 32. Main text keeps 7 figures + 3 tables = 10, renumbered Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–3; 22 items move to the SI as Supplementary Tables S1–S8 and Supplementary Figs S1–S14, with S15 added for the sixteen per-order panels split out of Fig. 11. Ten display items is generous for GCB but defensible for a paper with a decomposition, a random-structure comparison, a robustness grid and a projection-support diagnostic.

Abstract: 248 words, verified by word count on the exact submitted text (`wc -w` = 248). Single paragraph, no citations. Structure = 1 background sentence + 1 methods sentence + 5 result sentences + 1 significance sentence, which is the Nature-style shape the brief asked for, run slightly longer as GCB permits. It carries all four protected conclusions and the null-baseline qualification. Every numeral in it — 1,029; 2002–2024; 2.09; 83.1%; 37%; 1.36 with 1.22–1.52; 1.40 with 1.25–1.58; 0.85 with 0.76–0.95; P = 0.005; 1.157; 1.18; 0.980; 0.72 → 0.85; 0.27 → 0.41; 2.18 → 1.07; 36.9%; 27.9% — appears verbatim in the source manuscript, and the permutation and bootstrap values were checked directly against tables/tbl_null_models.csv (N3 clim_change null median 1.15696, P = 0.00508; N2 effort null median 0.97957, P = 0.005), tables/tbl_bootstrap_ci.csv and tables/tbl_v2_direction_overall.csv (East 237/642 = 0.36916; Northeast 179 = 0.27882). Two items from the source abstract were dropped rather than reworded to reach 250: the 79%-per-SD effort figure under publication-year dating (the 37% reduction conveys the same result and is the number reused in the Discussion) and the projection-support sentence (retained in full in Results 12 and the Discussion).

Citations: the draft keeps numbered superscripts; conversion to author–year is left to the main workflow as instructed. The 82-item reference list is unaffected, since no cited claim is deleted — only relocated.
risks: Results 7 loses 420 words, the single largest cut. The species-level and province-level analyses are companion strands, but a GCB reviewer may treat them as substantive. If the trait-imputation sensitivity or the migratory-stratified hand-wing-index result is demanded back in main text, the 393-word headroom covers roughly half of what would need to return. Mitigated by keeping one pointer sentence per moved claim, so nothing is left unsupported.

Table 4 (model adequacy) moves to the SI, which makes main-text Results 9 the only place where the proportional-hazards violation for effort (β = −0.211, P = 7.7 × 10⁻⁴) appears. That section is marked keep_full precisely to protect conclusion (iii); any later compression of Results 9 would orphan the conclusion and must be refused.

Extended Data Fig. 5 moves to the SI while the null-baseline qualification stays in main text. A reviewer may ask to see the null distributions among the main figures. The cleanest response is to add panel a of that figure to main Figure 1 rather than restore the whole SI figure, since the Fig. 1 legend already carries the 1.16 note.

Placing Methods after the Introduction means readers meet the completeness offset, the risk-set definition and the permutation-null design before any result. The compressed Results 1 assumes that ordering; if copy-editing moves Methods to the end, Results 1 needs about 40 words of restored explanation, which the headroom absorbs.

The 393-word buffer is not guaranteed. If GCB's counter includes table cell text or figure legends in the main-text total — practice varies by handling editor — the paper could exceed the cap despite the arithmetic. Fallback cut order, none of which touches a protected conclusion: Results 13 (−60), Results 12 (−40), Results 6 (−40), Results 11 (−30).

Splitting the sixteen per-order panels out of Fig. 11 into Supplementary Fig. S15 raises the SI figure count to fifteen and adds a renumbering step. The overall-plus-six-order-overlay panels retained in main Figure 6 must keep both sample sizes (records and species) or the χ² = 580.1 result loses its denominator.

Fig. 11's caveat that one species can contribute records in several provinces sits in the legend, not the body text. If that legend is trimmed in production, 237 of 642 and 36.9% could be misread as species counts rather than record counts. Flag to the production editor.

Two source-abstract items were dropped to reach 250 words (the 79% figure and the projection-support sentence). Neither is deleted from the paper, but an abstract-only reader will not learn that late-century projections are support-limited. If the editor wants that caution in the abstract, the cheapest trade is to drop the north-east percentage and shorten the east clause, freeing about 18 words.

Compressing thirteen Results subsections while forbidding any renumbering or rounding means the cut must fall entirely on connective prose. In Results 3, 8, 9 and 12 the number density is already close to one figure per clause, so the stated targets there are near the floor; if drafting shows they cannot be met, the deficit must be taken from Results 6, 10 or 13 rather than from any number-bearing sentence.
